overview.title: Chapter 1 opener: What is deep learning?
overview.main_topic: Introduction to the chapter that defines AI, machine learning and deep learning, and frames the hype around them
overview.central_idea: Chapter 1 sets out to give high-level definitions of AI, machine learning and deep learning, a gentle introduction to how machine learning works, and a sober assessment of deep learning's popularity and future. The opening paragraph motivates all of this: a practitioner must be able to separate real, world-changing developments from overhyped press releases.
overview.importance: This page establishes the stance of the whole book: deep learning is treated as a powerful technology that deserves clear definitions and critical judgement rather than hype. It also tells you what you will be able to do after reading the book — develop AI systems yourself.
learning_objectives: Know the three themes Chapter 1 covers: fundamental definitions, the principles behind machine learning, and deep learning's popularity and future potential
Understand why the authors begin with media hype and why a practitioner needs to recognize 'the signal amid the noise'
Preview the questions the chapter will answer: what deep learning has achieved, how significant it is, where it is headed, and whether to believe the hype

summary:
This is the opening page of **Chapter 1, "What is deep learning?"**. It is a chapter opener: a large chapter number, the title, a "This chapter covers" box, and the first paragraph of the chapter.

The box lists three things the chapter will do:

- give **high-level definitions of fundamental concepts** (AI, machine learning, deep learning — developed in sections 1.1–1.6, p.26–34),
- offer **a soft introduction to the principles behind machine learning** (how a model learns rules and representations from data, p.28–34),
- discuss **deep learning's rising popularity and future potential** (sections 1.7–1.12, p.34–39).

The opening paragraph starts from the media hype of the past decade. AI, machine learning and deep learning appear in countless articles, often in non-technical outlets, promising intelligent chatbots, self-driving cars and virtual assistants — a future painted sometimes as grim, sometimes as utopian, with scarce human jobs and most economic activity handled by robots or AI agents. The authors' point is practical: a machine learning practitioner must be able to **recognize the signal amid the noise**, telling world-changing developments from overhyped press releases. They add a motivating note — "our future is at stake" and you have an active role, because after reading the book you will be among those who can actually build these systems. The sentence breaks off with "So let's" and continues on p.26 with the questions the chapter will tackle: what deep learning has achieved so far, how significant it is, where we are headed, and whether to believe the hype.

How to use this page: read the bullet box as a map of the chapter, then keep the "signal amid the noise" theme in mind — it returns explicitly in section 1.10, *Beware of the short-term hype* (p.36), and section 1.11, *Summer can turn to winter* (p.38), and again in the book's closing reflections (p.621).

paragraphs.excerpt: Over the past decade, artificial intelligence (AI) has been a subject of intense media
paragraphs.what_it_says: AI, machine learning and deep learning have been heavily hyped in the media, including non-technical publications, with promises of chatbots, self-driving cars and virtual assistants and with visions ranging from grim to utopian (scarce human jobs, economies run by robots or AI agents). A practitioner must learn to distinguish genuine, world-changing developments from overhyped press releases. The authors add that the reader has an active role to play, because after this book they will be able to develop such AI systems themselves.
paragraphs.what_it_means: The authors are setting expectations before giving any definitions. Rather than selling the field, they ask the reader to adopt a critical stance toward claims about it — the same stance the chapter later applies in sections 1.10 and 1.11 when it discusses hype cycles and past 'AI winters'. The final sentence also reframes the reader: not as a consumer of AI news but as a future builder who is partly responsible for where the technology goes.
paragraphs.why_it_matters: Hype distorts both expectations and investment. Knowing what deep learning can and cannot do (defined precisely in the next pages) is the only reliable way to evaluate a claim. This paragraph is the book's first statement of a theme it returns to repeatedly: deep learning is a real revolution, but one that should be judged on its actual capabilities.

terminology.meaning: The broad field of automating intellectual tasks normally performed by humans; defined precisely on p.26.
The authors' phrase for separating substantive technical progress from exaggerated media and marketing claims.

connections: p.26: the sentence continues with the questions the chapter will answer and then defines AI, machine learning and deep learning (figure 1.1).
p.36: section 1.10 'Beware of the short-term hype' develops the warning given here.
p.38–39: section 1.12 'The promise of AI' gives the authors' own optimistic long-term view, balancing this cautious opening.

concepts.name: AI hype vs. real progress
concepts.definition: The gap between media and marketing claims about AI and what the technology can demonstrably do; the authors ask practitioners to be able to tell the two apart.
concepts.intuition: Headlines promise either utopia or doom; a practitioner looks instead at what a given system actually learned from what data, and how well it generalizes.
concepts.technical: The chapter later gives the tools for this judgement: precise definitions of AI, ML and DL (p.26–31), a mechanistic picture of how deep learning works (p.32–34), a list of concrete achievements (p.35), and a historical account of previous AI summers and winters (p.36–38).
concepts.significance: Expectations drive funding and adoption; unrealistic expectations have twice before led to 'AI winters' (p.38).
concepts.example: A press release announcing 'human-level' performance on one benchmark is not the same as a system that handles arbitrary real-world situations (see the discussion of local vs. broad generalization on p.600).
concepts.misconception: That being skeptical of hype means being skeptical of deep learning itself — the authors are strongly positive about the technology's long-term impact (p.39).

misconceptions.claim: Because the authors warn about hype, they think deep learning is overrated.
misconceptions.correction: The warning is about separating signal from noise. The same chapter argues that deep learning is a genuine revolution that is 'here to stay' (p.34) and that its long-term impact may be comparable to the internet (p.39, p.621).

takeaways: Chapter 1 covers three things: fundamental definitions, a soft introduction to the principles of machine learning, and deep learning's popularity and future potential.
AI has been the subject of intense media hype, with both grim and utopian visions; a practitioner must be able to recognize the signal amid the noise.
The book positions you as a future builder of AI systems, not merely an observer of the hype.

questions.answer: A step-by-step tutorial on building a Keras model
questions.explanation: The box lists exactly three items: definitions of fundamental concepts, a soft introduction to the principles behind machine learning, and deep learning's rising popularity and future potential. Hands-on Keras tutorials begin in later chapters, not in Chapter 1.

questions.question: According to the opening paragraph, why is it important for a machine learning practitioner to 'recognize the signal amid the noise'?
questions.answer: So that they can tell world-changing developments from overhyped press releases.
questions.explanation: The paragraph states this directly: amid intense media hype about AI, a practitioner needs to be able to distinguish genuinely significant developments from exaggerated claims.

questions.question: The paragraph describes two opposite ways the AI future is painted in the media. What are they, and what do the authors suggest about both?
questions.answer: A grim future and a utopian one (e.g. scarce human jobs, most economic activity handled by robots or AI agents). The authors treat both as part of the hype that a practitioner must learn to see through, rather than endorsing either.
questions.explanation: The text says the future is 'sometimes painted in a grim light and other times as utopian'. Immediately afterwards it insists on recognizing the signal amid the noise, implying both extremes are more noise than signal until judged against what the technology can actually do.

questions.question: What role do the authors say the reader will have after finishing the book?
questions.answer: They will be one of the people who can develop these AI systems — an active participant in shaping the future, not just an observer.
questions.explanation: The paragraph says 'Our future is at stake, and it's one in which you have an active role to play: after reading this book, you'll be one of those who can develop these AI systems.'

questions.question: Before reading on: write down, in one sentence each, your current understanding of 'artificial intelligence', 'machine learning' and 'deep learning'. After reading p.26–31, compare your definitions with the book's.
questions.answer: Open-ended. The book's definitions: AI is the effort to automate intellectual tasks normally performed by humans; machine learning is a subfield of AI in which programs (models) are learned from data rather than hand-written; deep learning is a branch of machine learning using successive layers of learned representations.
questions.explanation: Self-assessment: the chapter's first objective is to give high-level definitions of these fundamental concepts. Recording your prior beliefs makes the definitions on the following pages easier to retain and reveals which common misconceptions you held.
